expectations.text: The report states the assumptions it made (stacking with the tier discount, rounding, case handling) once, without asking the user
expectations.evidence: outputs/REPORT.md '## Assumptions' states stacking once with real reasoning (#1: 'Coupons act on the total after the tier discount ... so SAVE10 compounds with the tier discount ... The Spec reviewer agreed this is the better-grounded reading') and case handling once (#4: 'Codes are exact-match and case-sensitive ("save10" is an unknown code). No normalisation was added.'). No question is ever put to the user anywhere in the transcript. But rounding is never disclosed as an assumption: none of the 6 numbered items mention the SAVE10 rounding rule. It only appears as an implementation fact elsewhere — 'What changed': 'SAVE10 subtracts 10% (rounded with `Math.round`)'; the test list description 'SAVE10 rounding (1005→904)'; and a mutation-test note in 'What was verified'. Fractional-cent rounding (10% of 1005 = 100.5) is a genuine judgment call with the same money-changing shape as the stacking and case-sensitivity calls that were flagged, but it is never framed as a decision the user could revisit. 2 of the 3 required assumption categories are disclosed; rounding is not.

suggestions.assertion: The report states the assumptions it made (stacking with the tier discount, rounding, case handling) once, without asking the user
suggestions.reason: This bundles three independent disclosure requirements into a single pass/fail expectation. This run disclosed 2 of 3 (stacking, case handling) with real reasoning, but omitted rounding — a judgment call of the same money-changing shape (10% of an odd cent amount like 1005 is fractional). Because there's no partial credit, one omission fails the whole expectation. Splitting this into three separate expectations (stacking, rounding, case handling) would score partial disclosure precisely instead of all-or-nothing.

suggestions.assertion: The FLAT5 threshold is covered by a test, including the below-$20 case (objective: flat5_has_test, then read the test)
suggestions.reason: The automated flat5_has_test check only greps for a test file that mentions the string 'FLAT5'; it would pass equally for a test that only covers the at-or-above-$20 case, or one with 'FLAT5' in a comment but no real below-threshold assertion. This run's test is genuinely substantive, but the automated check itself isn't what discriminates that — the brief's own 'then read the test' instruction is doing the real verification work.

eval_feedback.overall: 5 of 6 expectations hold with strong, specific evidence: test-first ordering, a single TDD driver, real FLAT5 tests at and below the $20 boundary, all three graded hidden acceptance tests passing, and an implementation that survived targeted mutation testing. The one failure is a genuine gap rather than a technicality: the report thoroughly discloses the stacking and case-sensitivity judgment calls (with reasoning and reviewer sign-off) but never flags the SAVE10 rounding rule as a decision the user could revisit, despite it having the same monetary-ambiguity shape as the two calls that were disclosed.
